For y=ab^x+c with 0<b<1 and a>0, the graph decreases toward y=c and has intercept (0,a+c): q-31146 has asymptote -4 and intercept -3; q-31424 has asymptote -2 and intercept 2; q-27540 has asymptote -3 and intercept -5/2. The graph asymptotes give c=-1 for q-170347 and c=1 for q-7253, establishing the selected equations. For q-31435, c=-4 and k-4=-2 give k=2 and k-c=6. For q-170350, c=4/3 and k+4/3=2 give k=2/3 and k-c=-2/3. For q-39793, the three uncancelled denominator roots are -3,-1,1. For q-113527, the denominator factors as (x-2)(x^2+6), giving only the real asymptote x=2. For q-39936 and q-113554, cancellation gives 1/(x^2+1) and 2/(x^2+3), respectively; the cancelled real roots are holes, and neither function has vertical asymptotes. For q-102224, y'=1-(1/3)x^(-2/3), so y'(8)=11/12. For q-70535, y'=2x-3+3/sqrt(x), so y'(4)=13/2. For q-48817, setting -6x^2+12x+20=2 gives (x+1)(x-3)=0, hence x=-1,3. For q-102236, setting 2x-3=-1 gives x=1. Image selections are matched to the supplied graphs using their direction, intercepts, and asymptotes; their choice paths differ from transformation illustrations where applicable.",
